title: The Wheel

seo.title: Destiny matrix 10 — The Wheel: meaning of the arcanum
seo.description: The Wheel is arcanum 10: the energy of cycles and a feel for the moment. What 10 means in the destiny matrix, how it works at its best and at its worst.

meaning: A ten in the destiny matrix is the energy of the cycle and the turn: such a person’s life moves in circles rather than in a straight line, and what decides it is not years of even work but the rare moments when the wheel comes round and everything settles differently. What 10 means is living inside changing stretches, where a fall is followed by a rise, and luck and loss turn out to be two sides of one revolution.

The character of this energy is mobile and quick to sense things. The inner engine of a ten is neither will nor calculation but a feel for the moment: it catches what is about to sway and is there before the change becomes obvious to everyone else. Hence the main inner conflict — between wanting to steer events and knowing that the wheel will come round on its own. Being this arcanum means deciding again and again where your move is, and where you simply have to sit the turn out and not take the pause for a defeat.

In its strong version the ten is a navigator: it does not argue with the current but reads it and enters the new earlier than others, while the turn is only beginning. The weak version is the same character, sensitive to change but twisted into passivity: since so much is decided by chance, it seems that nothing needs changing and hoping is enough. The difference between them is not who gets more luck, but whether a person takes part in the turn of the wheel or watches it roll past.

From its neighbour The Hermit this arcanum differs in tempo and direction: the ninth goes inwards and ripens in silence, the tenth lives on the surface of the event and wins by the speed of its reaction. From Strength it differs in how it meets circumstances: the eleventh arcanum tames them with patience and gentle endurance, while the tenth feels the world as a game of chances, where a case caught in time is worth more than long endurance.

article.title: Arcanum 10 in the destiny matrix: The Wheel of Fortune
article.short: 10 in the destiny matrix is The Wheel of Fortune: the energy of cycles, turning points and the right moment. A person with the ten lives in turns: rise, peak, decline, a fresh start. The gift of the arcanum is a sense of timing and the ability to get up after a fall; its trap is waiting for luck instead of acting, and spending everything on the way up. 84% of people have the ten somewhere in their reading, and one in nine has it in the centre of the matrix.

seo.title: Destiny matrix 10 — The Wheel of Fortune: meaning of the arcanum
seo.description: Destiny matrix 10 is The Wheel of Fortune: rhythm, not luck. The four phases of a turn, where 10 appears, its tails, program 10, money and compatibility.

sections.h2: In short: what 10 means in the destiny matrix

ul: **The essence:** cycle, turn, the right moment. Not luck as such, but the rhythm within which luck happens.
**The gift:** noticing change before others do, stepping into something new at the right time, getting back up quickly after a failure.
**The trap:** waiting for things to “turn by themselves”; spending everything on the way up and dropping what was started on the way down.
**The task:** to find what stays the same while everything spins, and to meet the turn prepared.
**Where it is most common:** in the centre of the matrix (11.1% of people), in the karmic task D (8.9%) and in the month point, for everyone born in October.
**Where it never appears:** in point M, the entry of the karmic tail and of the relationship line, and in the spiritual purpose.

sections.h2: Rhythm, not luck
paragraphs: The name is misleading. Fortuna was the Roman goddess of chance, so the ten is often described as “the lucky one’s arcanum”. But the card means something else. Arthur Waite, the author of the best-known Tarot deck, wrote that behind this symbol lies “the **denial of chance** and the fatality which is implied therein”: neither blind luck nor the blind doom that would follow from it. For him the wheel stands for “the perpetual motion of a fluidic universe” and “the flux of human life”, and the essential idea of the card is **stability amidst movement**.

Long before the Tarot, the wheel of Fortune was described by Boethius. In The Consolation of Philosophy (6th century), Fortune says: “This is my power, this the endless game I play: I turn the wheel in its spinning circle and delight in bringing the lowest to the top and the top to the bottom. Climb up, if you like, but on one condition: do not count it a wrong when the rules of my game require you to come down.” Those two sentences hold almost the whole of the ten. The climb is legitimate, and so is the descent. Only someone who mistook the summit for a permanent address feels wronged.

In the destiny matrix, 10 means that life runs not in a straight line but in waves, and the most important things in it happen at the turning points. Everyone has ups and downs, but for a ten they are more visible, more frequent and more significant. So the main skill of the arcanum is not to stop the wheel (that is impossible), nor to ride it with your eyes shut, but to understand where in the turn you are right now and to act according to the phase.

Every wheel has a rim and a hub. A point on the rim is thrown now up, now down; the hub turns with the whole wheel but stays where it is. A ten in plus lives closer to the hub: circumstances spin, but the person has something that does not change with every turn, whether a craft, a principle, the people close to them or their own daily order. A ten in minus lives on the rim, where every turn is either a take-off or a disaster.

Benebell Wen, author of the book Holistic Tarot, calls The Wheel “the karma card” and offers an unexpected parallel: the unit circle from school trigonometry. Follow the height of a point running round the circle and you get a sine wave: crest, fall, trough, a new rise. No phase lasts for ever, and each one shows which will come next, if you know where you are on the curve.

sections.h2: What a person with the ten is like
paragraphs: Their life story is hard to tell in a straight line. Three cities, two professions, a business that closed, and a venture that unexpectedly grew out of a side job. Ask how it happened and you will hear “and then everything turned”. This is not necessarily chaos: often a single substance lies beneath the changing forms. The person sold, then taught selling, then started a business of their own: three different lives from the outside, one in essence.

A ten senses a change before it becomes obvious. An idea nobody wanted for a year is suddenly needed by everyone within a week, and the person with the ten is already standing next to it. They are not necessarily smarter or harder-working than the people around them. They simply notice sooner that the wind has changed, and are not afraid to turn while turning is still cheap.

The flip side is a poor tolerance for anything steady. A year without events feels like stagnation, and if life does not turn by itself, the person starts turning it by hand: quits a job “just because”, sets up a move, picks a quarrel in order to make up. From the outside it looks like inconstancy; from the inside, like an attempt to feel movement again.

And there is one more trait people value in the ten: it knows how to fall. Losing almost everything and standing on its feet again a year later is not heroism for this arcanum but a familiar phase. People with a strong ten often become the ones others turn to in a crisis: they know from experience that the bottom is also a point on the turn, not the end of the road.

sections.h2: 10 in plus and in minus: one wheel, two ways to ride it

head: In plus
In minus
rows: Sees the turn coming and steps into the new at the right time
Waits for things to “turn by themselves” and misses the moment
On the way up, saves and locks in the result
Spends everything on the way up and is left empty on the way down
Carries what was started through the decline
Drops the work as soon as it gets harder
Accepts change as part of the rhythm
Clings to what has outlived itself to the last, or changes everything for no reason
Notices a repeating pattern behind the “coincidences”
Blames fate for what they never took on
Gets up faster than others after a failure
Lives from one burst to the next, with emptiness in between

paragraphs: Plus and minus are not two different people but two ways of handling one and the same turn. The ten is knocked out of its rhythm by one of three things.

ul: **Waiting.** “If fate decides everything, why bother?” The chance slips past and is later explained as bad luck. This is the most common minus of the arcanum.

**Holding on.** An attempt to stop the wheel at the top: to fix a good period in place for ever, to ignore that conditions have changed, to defend what has already outlived itself. The turn happens anyway, only now as a collapse.

**Rushing about.** Change for the sake of change: a new goal before the old one is finished, motion instead of a path. In Waite, the reversed Wheel means not misfortune but “increase, abundance, superfluity”, and a superfluity of motion also knocks you out of rhythm. This is our reading of his list, not Waite’s own interpretation.

paragraphs: A separate word on gambling. The costliest form of the minus is mistaking the rhythm of life for roulette. A roulette wheel has no memory: “I’ve been unlucky for so long, so I’m due a win” is the classic gambler’s fallacy. The wheel of the ten speaks of cycles you can study, not of a bet that is bound to pay off.

sections.h2: The four phases of a turn, and what to do in each
paragraphs: The ten becomes useful in practice with one question: “where am I on the wheel right now?” Each phase has its own right tactics, and most of the mistakes of this arcanum are tactics from the wrong phase.

head: Phase
How to recognise it
What to do
The main mistake
rows: Doors open, offers get answers, effort pays off faster than usual
Step in, test with small stakes, respond quickly
Hesitating until the window has closed
Everything runs by itself, and it feels as if it will always be like this
Consolidate: save, put agreements on paper, build what will outlast the decline
Spending everything and taking on commitments on the assumption of endless growth
The same effort brings less, resistance grows
Cut back, finish what you started, save your strength
Dropping what you started, or taking the decline as a final verdict
Nothing moves, neither up nor down
Prepare: learn, repair, build reserves, and name in advance the sign of the next chance
Waiting for a “sign” without preparing anything

paragraphs: A decline is neither a punishment nor a malfunction but as much a part of the turn as the rise. Whoever understands this stops spending energy on resentment and spends it on preparation instead, and the next rise finds them ready. From the outside, that is exactly what the “luck” of the ten looks like.

sections.h2: Where 10 appears in the matrix and how to find it
paragraphs: The ten is one of the most widespread energies. Counting all birth dates from 1900 to 2026, 84.3% of people have it somewhere in their reading (across the arcana this share ranges from 13.4% to 85%). It turns up most often in the chakra map (57.3%) and in the reading by decades (44%). Of the main points, it is most often found in the centre: 10 stands there for 11.1% of people, which makes it, alongside 6 and 8, the most common centre of all.

paragraphs.h3: How to check in a minute

paragraphs: The first five points can be worked out in your head. Any number greater than 22 is reduced by adding up its digits.

ul: **A, the calling card (personality portrait)**: the day of birth. The ten is here for those born on the **10th and the 28th** (2 + 8 = 10).
**B, spiritual task**: the month. The ten belongs to everyone born **in October**.
**C, material task**: the sum of the digits of the year. The ten comes from the years **1900, 1999, 2008, 2017 and 2026**; for 1999 it comes via 28.
**D, karmic task**: the sum A + B + C.
**E, centre**: the sum A + B + C + D.

paragraphs: Example: 10.05.1988. A = 10, B = 5, C = 1 + 9 + 8 + 8 = 26 → 8, D = 10 + 5 + 8 = 23 → 5, E = 10 + 5 + 8 + 5 = 28 → 10. The ten appears twice, in the calling card and in the centre. The other points (the money and relationship lines, the tail, the chakras, the decades) are easier to [calculate in full from your date of birth](/by-birth-date).

There are two positions where 10 does not occur for any date at all: point M (the entry of the karmic tail and of the relationship line) and the spiritual purpose. The reason is arithmetic. Reducing a number by adding its digits does not change the remainder after division by 9, and the formulas for these two points always give a number with a remainder of 0, 3 or 6. So only 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 or 21 can stand there. Two consequences follow: the karmic tail never begins with a ten, and the relationship line never opens with one. If you come across a reading of “10 at the entry of the tail”, be aware that in Ladini’s classic scheme this placement does not exist.

sections.h2: 10 across the sections of the reading, one by one
paragraphs: Some of these topics have their own detailed pages on the site; the links are at the end of the items.

ul: **The centre**, also called the comfort zone. The balance of a ten in the centre rests on movement: it is at ease when life is changing and uneasy when everything has frozen, and it loses its footing if it waits for things to turn by themselves. Two arithmetical details: everyone with a ten in the centre has Manipura reading 10-10-20 in the chakra map, and a karmic tail of 15-20-5 or 6-20-14. In detail: [10 in the centre of the destiny matrix](/encyclopedia/position/center/10).

**The calling card, point A**: for those born on the 10th and the 28th. The first impression is of someone who turns up in the right place at the right moment and changes course easily. In detail: [10 in the calling card](/encyclopedia/position/day/10).

**Character and personal qualities** (17.7%): the person is hard to catch in one place; they sense before others that it is time to change course, and make plans not by the year but up to the next turn.

**Money**: the money channel and the point other charts mark with a dollar sign, the middle of the money line, R2. 25.2% of people have the ten in the money section. Income comes in waves (deals, seasons, lucky hits), and the main rule is to put a share aside at the peak, while there is something to put aside. In detail: [10 in the money channel](/encyclopedia/position/money/10).

**What opens wealth and resource** (14%): resources come not in a steady stream but in portions, through a lucky alignment of circumstances. They go to whoever already has the reserve, the paperwork and the decision in hand when the moment comes.

**Money after 40** (14%): the instinct for timing is better spent no longer on one-off lucky deals but on what keeps feeding you in a downturn too: investments, a stake in a business, letting out property.
**Karmic task before 40** (12.2%): not to put life on pause while waiting for “your hour”. The hour does come, but it catches off guard anyone who has done nothing to prepare for it.

**Relationships and the point under the heart** (R1, the partner point): a union with a ten lasts as long as the couple has shared plans and changes, while frozen relationships feel cramped to it. A difficult conversation is better scheduled than left waiting for a convenient moment. In detail: [10 in relationships](/encyclopedia/position/relations/10) and [10 under the heart](/encyclopedia/position/love_middle/10).

**Body resource** (18.9%): a ten’s strength also goes in circles: there are days when heavy work seems to do itself, and days when even simple things get bogged down. The winner is the one who does not argue with this rhythm but plans around it.

**Rest** (17.8%): what recharges a ten is whatever has not happened yet: an unfamiliar city, a new activity, a trip decided on in a day. The best rest for a ten is a small turn made with its own hands.

**The year.** If your personal year is a ten, it is a year of turns and short windows of opportunity: [10 for the year](/year/10). The general arcanum of 2026 is also 10 (2 + 0 + 2 + 6); read about it in [the destiny matrix for 2026](/year/2026).

sections.h2: The ten in the karmic tail: just four tails
paragraphs: The karmic tail is the triple M–N–D: the entry, the mechanism of the loop and the root. A ten never stands at M, so in the tail it appears only in the middle or at the root. There are only four such tails out of the 26 possible, and each of them always comes with the same number in the centre of the chart.

head: Tail
Where 10 is
How often
Centre for everyone who has it
The story
rows: the person walls in their world for the sake of security, and the wheel turns anyway
building “for ever” on a rotating foundation until the structure collapses
a picture of how the world ought to be runs into a turn again and again; the way out is to turn faith into a road of one’s own
the person turns every change of season into a final ending; the task is to prune, not to uproot

paragraphs: A ten in the middle of the tail is a mechanism: the loop is set off by a turn of circumstances to which the person responds out of habit. A ten at the root is a task: to learn to live through the changing seasons and keep what has already been grown.

The link works the other way too. If the ten stands in your centre, your tail is one of two: [15-20-5](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/15-20-5), the most common of all 26, found in roughly one person in ten, or [6-20-14](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/6-20-14). With 10 in the centre there are no other options. All the tails are [in the full list](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail).

sections.h2: Program 10: the loop the ten keeps repeating
paragraphs: A search for “program 10” usually means a ten in a karmic point of the chart. In the reading this is the section “Programs: what repeats in circles”: it reads the karmic task D as the source of the recurring theme, and the centre E as the state that keeps it going. 20% of people have the ten in one of these two points. How programs work in general is covered [in a separate article](/programs).
The loop of the ten is easy to recognise:

ol: Rise: everything starts working out, money and offers come on their own.
Peak: it feels as if it will be like this from now on; no reserve is built, and commitments grow.
Decline: the work is dropped rather than finished; energy goes into resentment.
Explanation: “bad luck”, “not the right time”, “that’s fate”.
Waiting: the person waits for the next rise, and it all happens again.

paragraphs: Wen writes that The Wheel can be “a foreshadowing that history will repeat itself”: “the past will become the future and there could be a sense of déjà vu.” The signs of the program are similar endings at similar intervals, and a life story that can be summed up as “and then everything turned again”.

The loop can be broken in two places. At the top, by the habit of consolidating: putting a share aside and getting agreements on paper while all is well. At the bottom, by the habit of finishing: completing what was started by a deadline set in advance, not when the excitement wears off. Neither requires faith in luck, which is exactly why both work.

If you are searching for a triple such as “10-20-10” or “18-10-10”, first check which line of your chart it stands in. In this calculation 10-20-10 occurs, for example, as a money line (L–R2–R), and 18-10-10 as a relationship line (M–R1–R). The same triple reads differently in the tail, in money and in relationships.

sections.h2: 10 in talents and profession
paragraphs: The talent line is B–P–K: the month of birth, the middle point and the inner point next to the centre. The section “Profession and work you love” sits on the same line. 19.4% of people have the ten here, and for those born in October it opens the talent line.

The talent of the ten is a sense of timing. Not “what to do” but “when”: when to enter a market, when to make an offer, when to close a deal, when to wind a project down. Hence the work that suits it is work where results depend on the moment and the season: trade and brokering, launching new products, project work, seasonal business, travel and events, crisis management, any fast-moving market. Work where every day repeats the one before smothers this gift.

Instead of a list of professions, here are three questions to ask of any job. Does it have seasons, cycles, windows of opportunity? Does the person who notices a change first come out ahead? Does experience build up from one turn to the next, or do you have to start from scratch every time? The more “yes” answers, the better the job suits a ten. And one condition, so that a lucky turn does not become a gambling story: test a new opportunity on a small scale first, with a loss limit you have agreed with yourself in advance.

sections.h2: The ten in the family line and in purpose
paragraphs: In the family-line points F, G, H and I the ten stands for 6–7% of people in each, and it tells a family story of ups and downs: there were generations who rose, and generations who started from nothing. From this story it is worth taking the skill of getting up after losses, but not the route itself. A person’s own task on this line is to make sure that those who come next inherit not another pit but what has been built up.

In the section on parents and children (18.4%) the ten is a house where every day is a party: fun and unpredictable, but harder on routine. A child next to it needs not only adventures but also things that always happen at the same time; a ten has to build such anchors on purpose.

In purpose the ten appears in the personal (6.4%), social (7.9%) and planetary (7.6%) purposes, but not in the spiritual one. Here its role is a guide through change: the person next to whom others find the courage to turn, and the one whose own example shows that a decline is followed by a rise.

sections.h2: The Wheel’s decade: at what age 10 takes the lead
paragraphs: In the reading by decades, the eight outer points of the matrix take turns leading a life from birth to 80. 44% of people have the ten leading at least one decade, and the point tells you which one.

head: Where 10 stands
Decade
How to tell
rows: A + B + C gives 10 after reduction

paragraphs: A decade like this is hard to live by a plan drawn up in advance: too much in it is decided by the turns. A different approach works: a plan with slack, keeping part of your money and time free, and knowing in advance what you would change everything for and what you would not. How the whole scale is read: [the reading by decades](/encyclopedia/position/years).

sections.h2: The Wheel of Fortune in a couple’s matrix: a union that lives in cycles
paragraphs: Compatibility is calculated separately from the personal matrices: the matching points of the two partners are added together and reduced to 1–22, giving a third matrix — the couple’s matrix. A 10 in it does not mean the same as 10s in both personal charts, and a match of arcana between partners says nothing about the union on its own.

Yuliana Lisovskaya, author of a book on compatibility by the destiny matrix, makes **cycles** the key of the 10 in a couple: rises and crises take turns, and this has to be accepted rather than fought. In the plus it is a lucky, sociable couple with a sense of a fated meeting; in the minus, a seesaw of “silence — conflict”, debts and a habit of blaming fate. Most often the 10 stands in the middle of the couple’s tail and in its attitude to money; what it means at each point is on a separate page about the 10 in compatibility.

sections.h2: Arcanum 10 in a woman and in a man
paragraphs: Gender plays no part in the calculation: the matrix is built only from the day, month and year of birth, so the ten is the same for a man and for a woman. The circumstances in which a person lives out their rhythm differ, but the arcanum itself does not. Readings like “a woman with a ten needs a reliable man” or “a man with a ten is destined to take risks” are stereotypes, not the meaning of the card.

The matrix does have male and female lines, but they are family lines, not the gender of the person whose chart it is. A ten in the male line (points F and H) speaks of ups and downs on the father’s side, in the female line (G and I) on the mother’s side, and this holds equally for a daughter and for a son.

sections.h2: The Wheel and the other cards of change
paragraphs: The ten is often confused with arcana that also speak of change. The difference lies in the kind of change.

head: Arcanum
What kind of change
How it differs from The Wheel
rows: an ending: a stage closes for good
The Wheel brings things back, so what went down will rise again; Death brings things to an end
the collapse of a false structure
The Wheel turns; The Tower breaks what refused to turn
awakening, a call, a review of one’s life
The Wheel is a turn of circumstances from outside; Judgement is a response from within
the consequences of one’s own decisions
for Wen, The Wheel is the wider order, “beyond the Seeker’s immediate control”, while Justice is human choice, “human-made” rules and their outcome
The World is a cycle gone through to the end and gathered into a whole; The Wheel is a cycle in motion

paragraphs: If the ten stands next to one of these arcana in your chart, see the page for that combination, for example [The Wheel and The Tower](/encyclopedia/combination/10-16) or [The Wheel and Death](/encyclopedia/combination/10-13).

sections.h2: Waite’s Wheel of Fortune: what the classic card shows
paragraphs: The classic card was drawn by Pamela Colman Smith for Waite’s deck (1909). In the middle is a wheel floating in the clouds. Around its rim run the Latin letters T, A, R, O: they are read both as TARO and as ROTA, Latin for “wheel”, and Wen notes that read anticlockwise they give TORA, the same word as on The High Priestess’s scroll. Between the Latin letters stand the Hebrew letters of the Divine Name. In the inner circle are four alchemical signs; Wen reads them as mercury, sulphur, salt and water.

At the top of the wheel sits a sphinx with a sword. For Waite this is the main image of the card: **equilibrium within movement**. He singled out for criticism versions in which the sphinx rests “couchant on a pedestal above” the wheel: that, in his words, “defrauds the symbolism by stultifying the essential idea of stability amidst movement”. The sphinx is not above the wheel but on it, and still in balance.

On the left a serpent slides downwards: Typhon, the god of destruction, whom Waite deliberately “presented … in his serpent form”. On the lower right a figure with a jackal’s head rises with the wheel: Hermanubis. Waite took Egyptian images, he said, because they serve the symbol, and stressed that this was no argument for an Egyptian origin of the Tarot: such symbolism is legitimate “when this serves our purpose, provided that no theory of origin is implied therein”.

In the four corners, on clouds, are a winged angel, eagle, lion and bull with open books. These are the “four Living Creatures” from the vision of the prophet Ezekiel; in Christian tradition they became the symbols of the four Evangelists, and in Waite’s deck the same four creatures appear again on The World. He explained them himself: the letters on the wheel show “the Divine intention within”, and the Living Creatures show “the similar intention without”. Later interpretations link them with the four fixed signs of the zodiac (Aquarius, Scorpio, Leo and Taurus), but that is not in Waite.

Waite was scathing about what others had written about the card. The occult explanations of The Wheel from the days of Éliphas Lévi onward are, in his words, “even for occultism itself—of a singularly fatuous kind”, while “the findings of common fortune-telling are better than this on their own plane”.

paragraphs.h3: How the wheel came into the Tarot

paragraphs: The Wheel of Fortune is one of the most popular images of the Middle Ages. The Carmina Burana manuscript (13th century), which records the verses “O Fortune, like the moon, ever changing” (Carl Orff set them to music in 1937), contains a miniature of the wheel with four figures. Their captions read Regnabo, Regno, Regnavi, Sum sine regno: “I shall reign, I reign, I have reigned, I am without a kingdom”.

On eighteenth-century Tarot cards, as Waite describes them, “nondescript” animals climbed and fell on the wheel, “one of them having a human head”, and at the top sat a winged monster with “a crown on head”. In the nineteenth century Éliphas Lévi replaced them with Egyptian figures: Hermanubis rising, the sphinx at the top and Typhon on the way down. Waite followed Lévi, but made Typhon a serpent and set the sphinx directly on the wheel.

sections.h2: Tarot card 10: what The Wheel means in a spread
paragraphs: The Wheel is the tenth card in all the major decks. Unlike Strength and Justice, which Waite swapped round compared with the Marseille deck, it has the same number everywhere.

In his list of divinatory meanings Waite gives the upright Wheel: **destiny, fortune, success, elevation, luck, felicity**. Reversed: **increase, abundance, superfluity**. Even the reversed card is not about bad luck for him, whatever the popular tables say.

Wen reads the card more broadly: a turning point, movement that has already begun. “What goes up will come down. What hits bottom will bounce up.” The card can mean a force majeure, a circumstance beyond a person’s control, or it can warn that history is about to repeat itself. For her the upright Wheel means life going with the flow, and the reversed Wheel means going against it. But even that is no failure: a result is possible, it will just take more willpower. Wen recalls the legend of the koi carp that swam up a waterfall and, for its persistence, became a dragon.

In the destiny matrix the card is not drawn but calculated from a date, so it is never reversed. The plus and minus of the ten in the matrix are ways of living the energy, not the position of a card in a spread.

sections.h2: How to live the ten in plus

ol: **Find your hub.** One or two activities, principles or rituals that do not change at the turns: a morning practice, a craft, the people close to you. While everything spins, they hold.

**The peak rule.** From every large inflow, whether of money, energy or attention, set aside a share for the decline straight away, without waiting for the end of the month. Saving is easy on the way up; on the way down there is nothing to save.

**Set the test for a chance in advance.** Write down which offer you would accept without a second thought: terms, amount, timing. When the chance comes, you will not have to guess whether it is a sign.
**The small cycle.** Try something new for two to four weeks with a limited stake, then decide. That way a turn becomes a test, not a leap.
**Finish by the calendar.** You may drop a project, but only at a checkpoint set in advance, not at a low moment. A decision made at the bottom is almost always worse than one made on schedule.

**Map your turns.** Write down the five to seven main turns of your life, with dates and what came before each. Your own rhythm becomes visible, along with the signals by which the next turn can be spotted early.
**The “fate or me” test.** When you feel like saying “bad luck”, ask yourself: what would I have done differently if I had known in advance? If there is an answer, it was not fate but a missed move.

sections.h2: Myths about the ten

ul: **“10 is the lucky one; everything just falls into its lap.”** The ten is lucky when a turn finds it ready. For Waite, the card actually denies chance.
**“The Wheel in minus means losses and failures.”** The minus of the ten is not bad luck but a way of handling change: waiting, holding on or rushing about.
**“10 is really a 1, because 1 + 0 = 1.”** In the matrix, numbers up to 22 are not reduced: 10 is an energy in its own right, not The Magician on a new turn of the spiral.
**“The ten can stand at the entry of the karmic tail.”** Never: point M only ever holds 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 or 21.
**“A ten year or a ten position promises a windfall.”** The matrix describes tendencies and themes, not events: it promises neither a windfall nor a loss.

sections.h2: What this article is based on

ul: **Calculation**: Natalia Ladini’s classic destiny matrix scheme. Shares and frequencies are our own count across all birth dates from 1 January 1900 to October 2026.
**Symbolism and divinatory meanings**: A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1910; 1922 reprint), Part II on the symbols and Part III on the meanings.
**Modern interpretation**: Benebell Wen, Holistic Tarot (2015), the chapter on Key 10.
**Compatibility**: Yuliana Lisovskaya, Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024), the section on the 10th energy.
**History of the image**: Boethius, The Consolation of Philosophy, Book II; the Carmina Burana manuscript (13th century).

**Our adaptation**: the four phases of a turn, the “hub” and the “peak rule”, the practices, and carrying all of this over to the positions of the matrix. This is a conclusion drawn from the sources, not a quotation from them.
